statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = len(nums) - k + 1, and for every i with 0 <= i <= len(nums) - k, r[i] equals the number of distinct values in the contiguous length-k window nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[i+k-1]; formally r[i] = |{ nums[j] | i <= j < i+k }|. All indices are 0-based, and each window is nonempty because k >= 1.
preconditions: nums is a slice of i64 with len(nums) >= 1; k is an i64; 1 <= k <= len(nums); len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.
